text.p: Paracelsus Healthcare Corp said on Wednesday it estimated its results for the third quarter would be well below expectations, and it might have to restate its financial results for the previous three quarters.

The hospital owner and operator said lower operating results of psychiatric and certain other Los Angeles metropolitan area hospitals, reimbursement accounting issues and the revision of allowances for some accounts receivable would hurt the third quarter.

Since certain Los Angeles hospitals were not expected to improve short- term, Paracelsus said its post-merger strategy would be to explore divesting them. It said it expected to treat these units as discontinued operations.
"In light of these factors, the company expects a significantly larger loss for the quarter than anticipated," Paracelsus said, adding that was reviewing the status of its bank covenant.
The company said an outside legal counsel was conducting an inquiry into its earnings shortfall in the quarter and into financial reporting practices in periods before the quarter.

The law firm of Wilmer, Cutler & Pickering would also conduct an inquiry into certain corporate reserve practices, under the supervision of a special committee appointed by the board of directors, the company said.

Based on the counsel's preliminary review, Paracelsus said it expected to restate its financial results and amend its quarterly reports on the Form 10-Q for the quarters ending December 31, 1995, March 31, 1996 and June 30, 1996.
"It is likely there will be adjustments relating to the use of reserves and recognition of certain bad debt expenses, collection expenses and facilities closure costs," it said.
Paracelsus was not immediately available for further comment.

There was no First Call mean earnings estimate for the third quarter. The company had a loss of $0.06 per share for the last 12 months and a loss of $0.13 per share for the first six months of fiscal 1996.
